budgetForm.endDateNeeded: The budget above ends on {{date}}, so this one needs an end date too
budgetForm.endDateAfterParent: The budget above ends on {{date}} — this one cannot run longer
budgetForm.adminScopeRequired: Name at least one person or group — a budget nobody manages appears in nobody’s “My Budgets”, and requests under it land with the budget above instead
budgetForm.shortensSubtree: Everything below this budget that runs longer — sub-budgets, projects and open requests — will end on {{date}} too.
budgetForm.resourceCapHint: The maximum everything under this budget may use in total.
budgetForm.managedByHint: These people or groups run this budget: they approve requests, change its settings and can pass parts of it on as sub-budgets. Their own projects here are created without approval.
budgetForm.requestersHint: These people or groups may create projects from this budget, without any say over it. Their projects wait for a manager’s approval unless auto-approve covers them. Leave empty to disable requests.
budgetForm.allowBudgetRequests: Also allow budget requests in addition to projects
budgetForm.allowBudgetRequestsHint: A requester can then ask for a budget of their own here and delegate further. Turn this off for a course budget that should only ever hold projects — managers can always create sub-budgets directly.
budgetForm.allowBudgetRequestsInactive: Only relevant once somebody may request here.
budgetForm.autoApproveNoRequesters: Nobody may request from this budget yet, so there is nothing to approve automatically. Add people or groups under <1>Access → “Who can request here”</1> first; this tab becomes editable as soon as somebody is listed.
budgetForm.autoApproveHint: Projects from the people under “Who can request here” are created immediately, without a manager, as long as this budget has room — and so are later changes to them that stay within it. What happens beyond that is the next switch.
budgetForm.allowBeyondOn: What auto-approve does not cover waits for a manager. Switch off to make it a hard limit.
budgetForm.allowBeyondOff: Off: what auto-approve does not cover is refused right away — nothing waits for a manager. The managers of this budget are not limited.
budgetForm.autoApproveExtensionsOn: A later end date applies at once, as long as it stays within the allowed term.
budgetForm.autoApproveExtensionsOff: Off: every extension waits for a manager, even though new projects are created at once.
budgetForm.individualOn: Each person gets at most the amounts below, summed over all their projects here — the setup for a course.
budgetForm.individualOff: Off: everybody draws from the whole budget until it is used up — the setup for a personal or team pool. Switch on to give each person a fixed share.
budgetForm.neverNeedApproval: Whatever is set here: giving resources back, ending a project sooner and changing its members never need an approval.
budgetForm.inheritsLimit: Use the limit of the budget above
budgetForm.inheritsLimitHint: For budgets that only structure the tree: the limit of the budget above applies, also when it changes later. Everything below shares that limit with the rest of the budget above. Managers, requests and automatic approval remain settings of their own.
budgetForm.inheritsLimitFromAbove: The limit of the budget above applies.

rootAdmin.title: OpenStack Sync Status
rootAdmin.triggered: Sync triggered. Refresh status in a moment.
rootAdmin.cliTitle: Managed projects, from the command line
rootAdmin.cliText: Every managed project carries the tag <1>{{tag}}</1>, plus its state, termination date and contact as tags. This command reads them straight from OpenStack, with your own credentials sourced, and prints them as JSON. Overdue ones e.g. with <1>jq 'map(select(.tags.termination // empty | . < (now | todate)))'</1>.
rootAdmin.preseedTitle: Some users could not be prepared in OpenStack
rootAdmin.preseedText: These people did not get their role. Their OpenStack account is ambiguous — most often the OIDC username differs from the email address. Assign the role to the correct account by hand, or correct the username; the next sync retries.

pending.label: Awaiting approval
pending.description: Requested, but nothing exists yet. Someone who manages the paying budget has to approve it first.

approved.label: Active
approved.description: Approved and running. The OpenStack project exists and the resources shown here are reserved for you.

change_pending.label: Change requested
change_pending.description: A change is waiting for a decision. Until it is approved the project keeps running on its previous limits, and those are what it costs.

rejected.label: Rejected
rejected.description: The request was turned down. Nothing was created and nothing is charged to the budget.

released.label: Released
released.description: This project was given up. Depending on the setup it is archived or deleted shortly; until then its machines keep running and it holds its budget. This cannot be undone.

archived.label: Archived
archived.description: Given up and shut down: nobody can log in any more, the machines are shelved, the floating IPs returned. Volumes and data are kept until the project is deleted for good.

imported.label: Imported
imported.description: Found in OpenStack but not managed here — it was created outside the self-service. It has to be adopted into a budget before it can be changed.

provisioning.label: Setting up
provisioning.description: Approved. The OpenStack project is being created — this usually takes a few minutes.
